clue.text: No time for stimulating stuff in symphony

indicators.note: 'no time' tells us the abbreviation for time must be absent from the word that follows

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
sexually stimulating writing or pictures

explanation.surface: A listener finds nothing arousing to enjoy in a symphony, short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the T from EROTICA leaves EROICA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eroica is the popular title of Beethoven's Third Symphony, so it is a named example of the genre.

clue.text: Anger going round in historic France after dropping litre as water measure

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so other letters sit within this word
dropping means letting fall away, so the abbreviation for litre is lost

blocks.note: rage is fierce anger
taken as written
Gaul was the Roman name for the region
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Fury spreads around ancient France once a litre goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaul is the Roman-era name for the land that became France; 'as' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain gauge is an instrument for measuring how much rainfall has collected over a period.

clue.text: Remained in 9 10, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: the answer to 9 across
the number itself, written out

explanation.surface: Someone stayed put inside a wild group of ten, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: '9 10' looks like a reference to two other answers, but only the 9 is a cross-reference; the 10 is just the word TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To indwell is to dwell inside or inhabit, so the past tense means stayed within.

clue.text: Service area uphill in region of India

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A motorway services sits on an upward slope in part of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service area' reads as a motorway stop, but it splits into a church service and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for its tea plantations.

clue.text: Curtailed stay having recalled no sight

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter of the word is dropped
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to stay with someone is to visit them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cut-short visit meant someone never got to see anything.
explanation.walkthrough: VISIT loses its tail to give VISI, then NO backwards gives ON: VISION.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is the faculty of seeing, the same meaning as sight used as a noun for eyesight.

clue.text: Imaginative person having charged item in travel document on railway

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
in a down clue, on means placed above, so one piece comes first

blocks.note: a visa permits entry to a country
an ion is an electrically charged particle
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A dreamer is charged a fee for something in their passport while travelling by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is someone with original ideas about the future, an inventive dreamer full of imagination.

clue.text: South Central: extremely short of top flats?

indicators.note: short of its top means missing its first letter, the top in a down entry

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
Cen. is a dictionary abbreviation for central
very means extremely

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes very small top-floor flats in a south-central district.
explanation.walkthrough: VERY loses its first letter to give ERY. In theatre, flats are the painted wooden panels that form the backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage flats are painted canvas panels, and together they make up the scenery of a play.

clue.text: Attempt to rise above the French generating rude looks

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the word is reversed
in a down clue, above places one piece before the next

blocks.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
les is the French plural for 'the'

explanation.surface: Trying to outdo the French produces some impolite stares.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogles are lecherous stares, the kind of leering glances considered impolite or offensive.

clue.text: Strange lights? Son hiding amidst white pillows, quaking

indicators.note: hiding amidst means tucked away among, so one letter sits inside the others
quaking means trembling, so the letters are shaken into new order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A frightened child hides among the white pillows, trembling at strange lights.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural form will-s-o'-the-wisp is the dictionary variant this enumeration uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A will-o'-the-wisp is a ghostly flickering light seen over marshes at night, caused by burning marsh gas.

clue.text: Very angry? Very quiet after inversion of character

indicators.note: one letter is turned upside down, and an upside-down M looks like a different letter

blocks.note: mild means gentle and very calm

explanation.surface: Someone flips from furious to calm as their character turns over.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the M of MILD upside down and it becomes a W, giving WILD. 'Character' here means a printed letter, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild is used informally for being furious, as in 'he went wild when he heard'.

clue.text: Bowling technique - ungainly style limiting runs - in style befitting maidens?

indicators.note: ungainly means awkward and clumsy, so the letters are put out of shape
limiting means hemming in, so one piece is enclosed by the others

blocks.note: in cricket a spin bowler makes the ball turn
letters to be rearranged
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator criticises a spinner whose awkward action restricts runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'maidens' look like maiden overs (overs with no runs scored), but the definition means unmarried women.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinsterly describes the manner of an unmarried woman, and maidens is an old word for unmarried young women.

clue.text: Faintly shining luminance occupying a long time before morning

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside something, so one piece goes within another
before places one piece ahead of the next in reading order

blocks.note: an age is a very long time
L is the physics symbol for luminance
a.m. marks the morning hours

explanation.surface: A faint glow lingers for ages before dawn breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: L as the symbol for luminance comes from physics, not crossword abbreviation lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam is an adjective for glowing or glinting with light, matching a dim shimmer of brightness.

clue.text: Legendary kingdom under the sea? Sees only rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes violently, so the letters are tossed into new order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diver searching for a sunken realm finds nothing but rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' reads as a noun on the seabed but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyonesse is the drowned land of Arthurian legend, said to lie beneath the waves off Cornwall.

clue.text: Look for note in shed

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a hut is a small shed
N stands for note

explanation.surface: Someone is told to search for a note left in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside HUT to give HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt is to search for something, a direct verb synonym of seeking.

clue.text: Omitting verse, papacy loves varying content of Revelation?

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so the abbreviation for verse is dropped from the letters
varying means changing, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for verse
letters to be rearranged once the verse is gone

explanation.surface: The papacy is said to favour editions of the Bible that skip a verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take V out of PAPACY LOVES and shuffle the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation describes the end of the world, which is the apocalypse; the book is also called the Apocalypse.

clue.text: Athenian statesman - a gentleman rising above ebbs and flows?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the title is reversed
in a down clue, above places one piece before the next

blocks.note: taken as written
sir is the title of a gentleman
the tide ebbs and flows

explanation.surface: A dignified statesman stands above the shifting tides of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristides the Just was a celebrated politician and general of ancient Athens in the fifth century BC.

clue.text: Battleground with elevated parts of buildings around border

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means lifted up, so the word reads from the bottom
around means surrounding another piece

blocks.note: rooms are the divisions of a building
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A battlefield overlooked by high buildings stands round the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedgemoor in Somerset was the site of the 1685 battle that ended Monmouth's Rebellion, the last on English soil.

clue.text: Redefined ‘elver’ ‘fishy’ in a delirious way

indicators.note: redefined means given a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dictionary editor rambles about the words elver and fishy as if in a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverishly means as if with a high fever, and delirium is the confused state such a fever brings on.

clue.text: More meaningless European politician at forefront of row

indicators.note: at the forefront means placed at the front, so these pieces come first

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
an MP is a Member of Parliament
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A Euro politician speaks even more hollow words from the front row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier, of words or gestures, means more lacking in substance or sincerity.

clue.text: Female with trouble in Portuguese song

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A woman with troubles pours them into a mournful Portuguese song.
explanation.definitionFit: Fado is the melancholy traditional folk song style of Portugal, especially Lisbon.

clue.text: Material drifting to shore - family gathering a good deal

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: fam is informal shortening of family
lots means a large amount

explanation.surface: A family gathers plenty of debris washed up on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is wreckage or floating debris that drifts on the sea and gets washed up onto beaches.

clue.text: Various pets tucked into food in Welsh town

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the letters are rearranged
tucked into means placed inside, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Assorted pets are tucking into their dinners in a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into food' paints animals eating, but it puts the shuffled letters inside CHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a market town in Monmouthshire on the Welsh border, known for its racecourse.

clue.text: Ham, hard and chewy? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
chewy meat is tough

explanation.surface: A diner complains that their ham is hard and chewy.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUGH loses its first letter to give OUGH. Ham here is a cut from the back of an animal's leg, not cured meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hough is a Scottish word for the hock or shin, and ham can mean the back of the thigh.

clue.text: Phone has bass even deeper?

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
a deeper note is a lower one

explanation.surface: A telephone line makes a voice sound deeper than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: The blower is British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is informal British slang for a telephone, from the old speaking tubes you blew into.

clue.text: Source of passion: succeeded in time of success

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a boom is a period of prosperity
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Passion springs from having triumphed during a prosperous period.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is the breast, traditionally regarded as the seat of the emotions and passions.

clue.text: Car company beginning to organise athletic event, ignoring university records

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
ignoring means leaving out, so the abbreviation for university is removed

blocks.note: Audi is a German car maker
the opening letter of organise
the discus throw is a field event
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A car firm starts organising a sports meeting with no university involved.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCUS loses its U to become DISCS.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio discs are sound recordings on discs, such as vinyl records or CDs, so records is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Sun currently - what will winter bring?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday or sun
currently means at present

explanation.surface: Today it is sunny, but someone wonders what the winter weather will bring.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is the characteristic weather of winter, the cold season's typical precipitation.

clue.text: Both sides in card game skipping last turns

indicators.note: skipping the last means the final letter of the game is missed out
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
right and left are both sides

explanation.surface: Both partnerships in a card game keep missing the last trick.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIST without its T is WHIS, and R and L go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirls as a verb means spins or rotates rapidly, which is what turns means here.

clue.text: Recall? Recall part of early Rome, maybe

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters sit within the following words
to recall is literally to call back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of early, all of Rome and the start of maybe

explanation.surface: Someone tries to call to mind something about early Roman history.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Recall' is the instruction to read backwards; the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory is the faculty of recalling things, so the noun names the ability behind the act.
